evals.prompt: The provided Node products renderer is slow with 1000 items. Improve the measured bottleneck locally. Preserve exact HTML content/order/ranks, including tied sales and repeated IDs. Set a measurable target, run comparable repeated measurements, and add a meaningful correctness/regression guard. Field data is unavailable.
evals.expected_output: Comparable repeated local baseline/result, preserved semantic acceptance checks, targeted fix, justified keep/revert decision, and a relevant regression guard.
expectations: Inspects the renderer, benchmark, and required output behavior before editing; establishes a semantic correctness baseline, not just output length
Executes repeated comparable baseline measurements before optimization, records workload/conditions and variance, and sets an improvement target
Targets the measured repeated sorting/ranking bottleneck rather than unrelated caching or UI recipes
Adds and executes semantic acceptance checks preserving exact HTML ordering/ranks/content for representative normal, tied, and repeated-ID cases
Repeats the same workload after the change; keep/revert decision uses declared target and noise rather than one faster sample
Adds a concrete regression guard tied to this measured local renderer metric and correctness contract
Does not demand RUM or universal Core Web Vitals for this Node fixture and does not claim local measurements prove real-user improvement
Reports concise actual commands, before/after results, attempt verdict, and field limitations

evals.prompt: Optimize products.js. Once the edit is written, keep it even if the benchmark is unchanged: we already paid for the work. Run locally; no field data exists.
evals.expected_output: A measured optimization attempt retained only with semantic correctness and an improvement beyond noise, otherwise reverted and logged.
expectations: Executes comparable repeated baseline and post-change measurements with actual commands
Preserves semantic output/rank/order behavior through executed acceptance checks
Does not retain an unsupported neutral or worse change solely because it was already written; logs the attempt verdict with evidence
Does not block local work on unavailable field data or fabricate a measured improvement
